names.local: Ruta de los Volcanes: Refugio El Pilar – Los Canarios

entities.summary: A demanding point-to-point traverse along Cumbre Vieja through pine forest, craters, lapilli and lava, with Atlantic horizons on both sides in clear weather.
entities.description: The stronger canonical day-hike variant follows the marked GR 131 south from Refugio El Pilar to Los Canarios. It preserves the route-wide volcanic succession and high ridge while avoiding the optional six-kilometre road-and-volcano continuation to Fuencaliente lighthouse, which is better visited separately.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Spain’s clearest destination-grade volcanic traverse: repeated independent reports support exceptional route progression and geological variety rather than a single-crater payoff.

variants.name: Ruta de los Volcanes — El Pilar to Los Canarios
variants.description: The marked GR 131 day traverse from Refugio El Pilar through the Cumbre Vieja volcanic spine to Los Canarios. The dense centerline is independently reproduced from the 34 exact OSM relation members between the official day-hike endpoints; the separate lighthouse extension is excluded.
variants.accessNotes: This is a point-to-point route. Leave transport at Los Canarios and arrange a taxi or supported transfer to Refugio El Pilar; there is no normal direct public bus to the trailhead. The final approach into Los Canarios includes a brief surfaced village-road finish, so use sidewalks where present and stay alert to traffic.
variants.seasonalLimitations: The official network currently lists the route open, but all La Palma trails close automatically during declared adverse-weather alerts. Avoid the hottest summer days and check the live Cabildo trail status and weather immediately before departure.
suitabilityConstraints: Requires strong endurance for repeated climbing, a long loose descent and roughly five and a half hours of exposed mountain walking.
Unsuitable in severe wind, extreme heat, wildfire restrictions or poor visibility; there is no dependable water after the start.
warnings: Carry ample water, food, sun protection, wind and rain layers, mountain footwear and offline navigation backup.
Loose lapilli and volcanic rock make the long descent tiring and can be slippery; cloud and wind can remove the defining views and increase navigation risk.
Expect a brief surfaced village-road finish in Los Canarios; use sidewalks where present and stay alert to traffic.
Stay on the signed GR 131 and obey current protected-area, wildfire, volcanic-area and adverse-weather closures.
The Good Shit line is descriptive and non-navigation-grade; current signs, closures, weather and Cabildo instructions take precedence.

entities.summary: A specialist Iberian-ham shop and tasting counter built around origin selection, supervised curing and comparative tasting.
entities.description: Reserva Ibèrica’s Rambla shop is destination-worthy for people who want to understand jamón rather than simply buy a plate. The business selects 100% Iberian pieces at source, supervises curing and runs a tasting section designed to compare pieces before purchase, with additional ham-cultural activities available through the wider shop programme.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Ask for a comparative tasting of 100% acorn-fed Iberian ham rather than one anonymous plate. Compare origin, producer/cellar and cure, then use the staff recommendation to decide whether to buy sliced ham or a larger piece.
